title: fix(service-datasource,metadata-core)!: the datasource-admin plugin reads environment rows only; a legacy organization-scoped datasource row is neither restored nor served (ADR-0131 D6)
body:
Fixes #22835
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## Summary

`DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` now reads the environment's stored `datasource` rows only. This is the ADR-0131 D6 read narrowing that #15206's C5 applied to every metadata read, carried to `@objectstack/service-datasource`, which S5's enumeration missed. A row stored in a legacy organization's layer is no longer restored at boot, served by the datasource-admin door or the metadata read door, pooled, updated or deleted by this plugin. The boot report `[metadata_org_scoped_unserved]` keeps naming it, and it stays at rest: neither deleted nor rewritten (#22011 A).

This makes the pending v18 note `.changeset/15206-reads-environment-only.md` ("served by no read and loaded by no boot") true for `datasource`. That note is not edited. #21922's "code wins on collision" restore design is unchanged.

Classes, positions and function names only (security card).

## What changed

- **One predicate, moved, not copied.** `isLegacyOrganizationRow` was module-private in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`. It moves verbatim to `packages/metadata-core/src/legacy-organization-row.ts` and is exported from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which both `objectql` and `service-datasource` already depend on (no new edge). `metadata-core` had no equivalent (searched for organization-row predicates). `objectql`'s three binder call sites now import it, unchanged, and the private copy is deleted.
- **Every read of a stored datasource row in the plugin goes through one helper.** The new private `findEnvironmentRows` (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts`) runs a `find` on `sys_metadata` (type `datasource`, state `active`, optionally one name, system context) and drops each row `isLegacyOrganizationRow` names. Census of the plugin's reads of stored rows, each now behind it:
  - `loadDatasourceRows`: the boot restore (`restoreRuntimeDatasources`);
  - `loadDatasourceRow`: the by-name read behind cluster convergence (`convergePool`) and the `/meta` datasource projection (`applyMetadataDoorWrite`);
  - `persistDatasourceRow`: the existence probe behind admin create and update;
  - `deleteDatasourceRow`: the existence probe behind admin remove.
- **By-name reads moved from `findOne` to a filtered `find`.** A single row picked by the store could be the legacy one while the environment's row exists. `findOne` leaves the plugin's private engine slice type (`DataEngineLike`), where it is now unused.
- **The plugin's other reads** (`listDatasourceRecords`, `getDatasourceRecord`, `countBoundObjects*`) read the MetadataService, not `sys_metadata`. They stop serving the legacy row because the restore no longer registers it. The measurement below shows this; hypothesis 3 holds.

## Measurement: real boot, before and after

Showcase via `bootShowcase` over a database file. Two `datasource` rows were stored with system context between two boots: one legacy organization-scoped, one environment. Readings come from the second boot.

| Reading | Before (`d489318714`) | After (`fccd98aea0`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| datasource-admin door: by name, list | 200, listed | 404, absent |
| metadata read door: by name, list | 200 (the legacy body), listed | 404, absent |
| live pool from the legacy row | opened | none |
| environment row: both doors, pool | 200, 200, pooled | 200, 200, pooled (unchanged) |
| boot report `[metadata_org_scoped_unserved]` | names the legacy row | names the legacy row |
| admin create under the legacy row's name | 400 "already exists" | 201; writes an environment row, legacy row untouched |
| admin remove under that name | 204, and **the legacy row was deleted** | 204; removes the environment row only, legacy row kept |

The last row is the same missing predicate on a write path's existence probe (`deleteDatasourceRow`). The same fix closes it.

## Pins

- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/datasource-restore-environment-rows.dogfood.test.ts` (new): a real boot, a restart and both doors. Three cases:
  - Premise and control: both rows are at rest, and the boot report names the legacy row.
  - Neither door serves the legacy row (404 by name, absent from both lists) and no pool opens from it. The environment row is served and pooled.
  - The writes' by-name reads never reach the legacy row: an admin create and remove under its name write and remove an environment row of their own, and a `/meta` save under the name is what the admin door then serves. The legacy row equals its stored bytes at the end.
- `packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/datasource-admin-plugin.test.ts`, describe `[#22835]` (two cases, on the file's existing `sys_metadata` double):
  - The restore registers and pools environment rows only. A row whose `organization_id` is the empty string counts as the environment's, per the one predicate.
  - With a legacy row inserted first under the same name as an environment row, the `/meta` projection, admin update, remove and create all reach the environment row, and a legacy-only name is neither registered nor pooled. The legacy row stays byte-equal.
- `datasource-system-context.pin.test.ts`: population count moved from `findOne` to `find` (5 reads); the system-context assertion is unchanged.
- `packages/metadata-core/src/legacy-organization-row.test.ts` (new): the predicate's truth table.

## Ablation (direction observed: red, as expected)

- Committed state `fccd98aea0`, mutated with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. In `findEnvironmentRows`, the anchor `.filter((row) => !isLegacyOrganizationRow(row));` was replaced by a filter that keeps every row, which reproduces the pre-fix reads.
- The anchor count went 1 to 0 and the marker 0 to 1. Blob `ed525af25cfd` became `f7140c73d786`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-datasource build`, then `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/service-datasource ABLATION-22835` found the marker present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`.
- Unit pins (`-t 22835`): **2 failed**. Readings: the legacy row was registered at restore, and the projection served the legacy body.
- Dogfood pin: **2 failed, 1 passed** (the premise control). Readings: the admin door answered 200 for the legacy row, and the admin create answered 400 "already exists".
- Restore: `ablation-replace --restore` then `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`. The blob equals HEAD (`ed525af25cfd`), `git diff HEAD` is empty and the tree is clean. After a rebuild, the preflight with `--absent` confirms the marker is absent from all 24 built files.

## Tests and gates

Head `b02b3f8c16` is a merge of `origin/main` `eed637c09f` (four commits, none touching these packages), plus a comment-only trim of the dogfood header.

- `@objectstack/service-datasource`: `vitest run`, 42 files and 765 tests passed. `typecheck` exit 0, and `tsc --listFiles` includes both edited test files.
- `@objectstack/metadata-core`: `vitest run`, 17 files and 386 tests passed. `typecheck` exit 0, covering the new test through both tsconfigs.
- `@objectstack/objectql`: the 16 `src/plugin*.test.ts` files plus `hook-binder-package-scope.test.ts`, 17 files and 158 tests passed. `typecheck` (including `check:test-typecheck`) exit 0.
- `@objectstack/dogfood`, isolated project: this pin plus the four sibling datasource files (`datasource-restore-code-wins`, `datasource-meta-door-reaches-admin-door`, `meta-door-code-datasource`, `external-import-code-datasource-namespace`), 5 files and 28 tests passed at `6e19243562`. The pin was re-run at `b02b3f8c16`: 3 of 3 passed. Dogfood `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 and lists the new file.
- Build: the dogfood dependency closure was built with turbo (63 tasks) after the merge.
- Lint: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the 8 edited TS files reported 8 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so untouched files cannot move. A repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 70 commands at `b02b3f8c16`, a superset of the 46 named at dispatch. All 70 ran sequentially, with the exit code captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation: 70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: eight unrelated packages unbuilt). After building them it re-ran and exited 0.
  - Verdict lines: `check-adr-0087-registration` reports 1 declared-breaking changeset, carrying its disposition. `check-empty-changeset` reports no foreign changeset modified. `check-changeset-no-major` reports no `major`.

## Changeset

`.changeset/22835-datasource-reads-environment-only.md`:

- Bumps: `@objectstack/service-datasource` minor (the narrowing), `@objectstack/metadata-core` minor (the new export), `@objectstack/objectql` patch (the import, no behaviour change).
- Carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with a FROM to TO row.
- ADR-0087 disposition: not-required (already-registered `metadata-read-organization-scope-retired`). That entry already retires every read of an organization-scoped row, boot hydration included.

## Line budget

+325 / -38 across 9 files against the merge base. Source is +59 / -36: `metadata-core` +24, `objectql` +4 / -11, `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` +31 / -25, mostly comments.

The advisory total of 300 is exceeded by the real-boot pin, 164 lines. It boots twice, mounts the admin routes and reads both doors and the store; its sibling datasource dogfood files run 250 to 300 lines.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- `metadata-protocol`'s `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows` re-checks the same row value inline instead of importing the predicate. That is a second spelling in a third package, though `metadata-protocol` depends on `metadata-core`. It is outside this claim's file surface. Carrier: none.
- No `objectql` test pins the hook and action binders' skip of a legacy organization row. This PR moves that predicate without changing it. Carrier: none.

## Contract review

This PR owes one contract-review-tier review before the queue (`Clause-②` narrowing), to be arranged by the seat.
